carry.method: Second-nearby NYMEX WTI holding return over each contract cycle (roll-free), carry = (C1 - C2) / C2 on the first day after expiry, long when carry exceeds the median of all prior months, else flat. Non-overlapping monthly windows.

carry.verdict: Months with carry above its prior-months median beat the rest significantly over the full sample (one-sided p = 0.018); the true sign split (backwardation vs contango) agrees (p = 0.015). After 2007 the spread is not distinguishable from zero (p = 0.27), but that test had only 67% power against the pre-2007 spread and the pre/post spread difference is not significant (p = 0.26); the rank correlation, with 82% power, fell from 0.20 to -0.03 (difference p = 0.0210). The Sharpe gain of timing over buy-and-hold is not significant (Ledoit-Wolf p = 0.11 full sample, 0.57 after 2007), and as a sign predictor it does not beat always-long over the full sample. No reliable modern-era edge is demonstrated; how much of the pre-2007 effect survives is not resolved by this sample.

sign_split.definition: carry > 0 (backwardation) vs carry <= 0 (contango); long when carry > 0

power_post_2007.statement: After 2007 (206 months) the spread test could only detect a spread of 3.47%/month or more (one-sided 5%, 80% power); it had 67% power against the pre-2007 spread of 2.92%/month, so a null spread there is weak evidence of decay. The rank test (two-sided 5%) could detect a correlation of 0.200 and had 82% power against the pre-2007 rank correlation of 0.204.

analytic.formula: P(same sign) = 1/2 + arcsin(rho)/pi for jointly normal labels with correlation rho

leak_anatomy.conclusion: Under a pure random walk the newest leaked training label agrees in sign with the test label 79.5% of the time (1/2 + arcsin(0.8)/pi), with no information about the future. On synthetic i.i.d. returns a 1-nearest-neighbour model trained without the purge scores 72.4% (gross Sharpe 3.67); its nearest neighbour is the newest row in 60% of decisions, and on those it scores 82.6% (a little above the unconditional 79.5%: the newest row is nearest when its one unshared return is small, which makes the two labels even more alike). A 20-tree random forest scores 66.7% with a gross Sharpe of 2.85 on noise, against the retracted model's 67.2% and 2.47 after transaction costs. With the purge the same models score 50.4% and 50.8%. Block-shuffled real CL=F returns give the same picture (72.9% leaked vs 49.7% purged). Real 5-session returns rise 53.6% of the time, so the no-skill accuracy there is each run's base rate, not 50%: 10 of 10 leaked runs and 0 of 10 purged runs beat their own base rate at 5%. The shuffled runs reuse the same returns, so they are not independent samples and their pooled tests overstate the evidence. The retracted Sharpe was the label overlap, not a forecast.

supply_study.method: Each event's path: peak = highest close over sessions 0-19, settle = close at session 10, both vs the mean close of the 5 sessions before day 0 (EIA RWTC daily spot). The placebo applies the identical statistics to every non-event session between the first and last event. p_value_vs_placebo: two-sided resampling test, 20000 groups of n random placebo dates (with replacement) vs the group's median; p_value_vs_year_matched_placebo: the same with each event's draw taken from placebo dates of its own calendar year; mann_whitney_p: two-sided rank test vs all placebo dates (placebo paths overlap, so it is approximate); ci_*: 95% percentile bootstrap of the group median (10000 resamples). Values at the event table's 0.1% resolution; ties count against the hypothesis. The tests treat a group's events as independent draws; events listed in overlapping_events share sessions, so they are not.

placebo.exclusion: sessions within 19 of an event (its base, window or settle would touch the event) are excluded

supply_study.conclusion: On a random non-event date the same statistics are +5.4% (peak) and +0.7% (settle): a 20-session maximum is positive on 87% of ordinary dates, so a group's median peak only means something relative to that. Announced or physical supply removal >0.5 mbpd (n=21): median peak +12.1%, settle +4.3% (p = 0.0005 / 0.0445 vs placebo; 0.0015 / 0.1027 year-matched): it differs from an ordinary date on peak (above). Geopolitical threat, no supply removed (n=10): median peak +4.0%, settle +0.5% (p = 0.4897 / 0.9443 vs placebo; 0.6419 / 0.9564 year-matched): it is indistinguishable from an ordinary date. Supply removal vs threat-only directly: p = 0.0309 (peak), 0.3874 (settle). Above the unmatched placebo at 5% but not the year-matched one: Announced OPEC(+) production cut (n=7, peak p = 0.0264 vs 0.0898 year-matched). Caveats: event dates and groupings were chosen with hindsight; the groups overlap; some events are close enough that their windows share sessions (hurricane_katrina_2005 and hurricane_rita_2005, 19 sessions apart; saudi_russia_price_war_2020 and opec_record_cut_2020, 24 sessions apart; opec_cut_2023 and iran_tanker_seizure_2023, 22 sessions apart; lebanon_hezbollah_2024 and iran_israel_oct_2024, 6 sessions apart), so members of a group are not all independent; and these p-values are not adjusted for the number of groups tested (see data/research_ledger.json).

ledger.method: One row per tested hypothesis; statistics and p-values read from the named artifact fields (or computed from them by the formula in `test`). Status uses the p-value as the test was run (alpha 0.05; 0.05-0.10 inconclusive). Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and Holm adjusted p-values are computed across every row with a p-value, on p_two_sided (the directional one-sided p doubled, capped at 1). t_equivalent = normal quantile of p_two_sided; clears_hlz_t3 applies the Harvey-Liu-Zhu (2016) t > 3 hurdle.
